The value of e is approximately 2.718281828459045, which is a non-terminating and non-repeating decimal. In other words, there is no exact fraction (p/q) such that p/q = e for any integers p and q.

Since Euler's number does not have a finite or repeating decimal representation, it cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers, making it irrational.

To summarize, Euler's number is irrational because it cannot be represented as a simple fraction, even though it has a well-known approximate value.
